sections.title: Recognition
sections.text: Leccinellum crocipodium has an ochre-yellow to brown cap, velvety at first and often cracked with age. The tubes and pores start lemon yellow and become olive grey; they may brown when pressed. The stem is spindle-shaped and vertically ridged, pale to yellow, with small scales that brown with age. Their alignment can resemble a net, but it is not a true reticulation.

sections.title: Cut surface and useful characters
sections.text: The flesh is whitish to cream; when cut it may turn pink and then black. The spore print is olive-brown. The colour sequence varies among specimens, and the scaly stem should not be described as reticulated.

sections.title: Habitat and season
sections.text: This ectomycorrhizal species grows with broad-leaved trees, especially oak and beech. It fruits mainly from July to November, depending on climate and region.

sections.title: Lookalikes and safety
sections.text: Other boletes with yellow pores or a dotted stem may look similar. The DGfM positive list considers it edible after sufficient cooking; this advice does not replace identification and reflects the German source. DGfM also marks it as particularly protected and RL3 in Germany. Check local rules before picking.

traits: Cap brown, yellow-brown to cinnamon, velvety, often cracked or tessellated at maturity
Pores small, sulphur yellow to beige, turning olive and ochre-brown when pressed
Spindle-shaped, vertically ridged stem, cream to pale yellow, with scales that brown with age; no true net
Whitish to cream flesh that may turn pink then black when cut · olive-brown spore print
Under broad-leaved trees, especially oak and beech · July to November
safetyNote: DGfM lists it as edible after sufficient cooking and marks it as particularly protected (§) and RL3 in Germany. Protection categories are regional; check local rules and have the identification confirmed.
